findings: (a) SHIPPED VOICE SURFACE = DICTATION ONLY, INPUT ONLY. Claude Code ships `/voice` voice dictation: push-to-talk (hold Space) or tap-to-record, speech transcribed live into the prompt input at the cursor position, mixed with typing. It is not a voice 'mode' with spoken replies. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation

(a) CONFIRMED NO VOICE OUTPUT IN CLAUDE CODE (primary Anthropic source). Anthropic's Help Center FAQ: 'Can I use voice mode with Claude Cowork or Claude Code? ... In Claude Cowork and Claude Code, dictation is available but voice mode isn't.' Full-duplex spoken conversation exists only in the Claude chatbot apps (iOS/Android/Desktop/web), not Claude Code. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11101966-use-voice-mode

(a) Voice dictation constraints (primary): requires a claude.ai account sign-in (unavailable with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN/apiKeyHelper, Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry); requires a local microphone (fails in cloud sessions and SSH); WSL needs WSLg; audio is streamed to Anthropic servers, not processed locally; transcription does not consume tokens or count toward /usage. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation

(a) Voice dictation surface and config: CLI (`/voice`, `/voice hold|tap|off`), persisted via settings `voice.enabled`, `voice.mode`, `voice.autoSubmit`; keybinding `voice:pushToTalk` in `~/.claude/keybindings.json`; language via the shared `language` setting. The Claude Code VS Code extension also supports dictation (same claude.ai requirement; unavailable in Remote/SSH/Dev Containers/Codespaces). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation

(a) Voice CAN reach a background session, still as user text: 'In hold mode, dictation also works in agent view. Hold your push-to-talk key while the dispatch input or a peek-panel reply is focused to dictate to a background session.' https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation

(a) The public launch was branded 'Voice Mode' (TechCrunch, 2026-03-03; announced by Anthropic engineer Thariq Shihipar, ~5% then ramping) but it is the same push-to-talk dictation: '/voice to toggle it on, then speak your command.' No spoken-response capability was described. https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/03/claude-code-rolls-out-a-voice-mode-capability/

(a) Critical for the dsh-openai-live design: because Claude Code dictation writes into the human's OWN prompt input, every voice-originated message in Claude Code today is user-authored by construction. Claude Code ships NO mechanism that attributes voice to a distinct producer identity. There is no first-party TTS/read-aloud; that is only third-party Stop-hook projects or an open feature request. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation ; https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/79542

(b) PATH 1 — MCP CHANNELS (shipped, research preview): an MCP server declaring the `claude/channel` capability emits `notifications/claude/channel` and pushes events into an ALREADY-RUNNING session, opt-in per session with `claude --channels plugin:<name>@<marketplace>` (or `--dangerously-load-development-channels` for dev). Official channels: Telegram, Discord, iMessage, fakechat demo. Requires Anthropic auth; org gating via `channelsEnabled` / `allowedChannelPlugins`. This is the closest published analogue of an external push into a live coding session. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference

(b) Channel delivery semantics: events queue in order and are delivered on the next turn if Claude is busy ('delivered together on the next turn and handled as a group'); a channel start-up notice states messages 'inject directly in this session'. Two-way channels expose a normal MCP `reply` tool for outbound; a trusted channel can opt into permission relay. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference

(b) PATH 2 — CROSS-SESSION MESSAGING (shipped, v2.1.224+ macOS/Linux/WSL2, v2.1.234+ native Windows): tools `ListAgents` (alias `ListPeers`) and `SendMessage`, plus an actual INBOX SOCKET per session. The docs say to read this section 'when you want a script or hook to post into a session'. Socket path is in `/status` (`Peer address`, prefixed `uds:`) and is exported to hooks and Bash as `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET`, with a per-session `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging

(b) The cross-session socket IS a documented external-injection ingress: a non-Claude process (script/hook/Bash command) opens the Unix domain socket (named pipe on Windows), optionally sends `{"type":"auth","token":"<CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN>"}` as the first line (optional on macOS/Linux, required on Windows), and posts a message. Connections idle >30s are closed, so build the payload first. Inbound is gated by `crossSessionInbound` = accept|hold|refuse, `dialogExpiry`, and `isolatePeerMachines`. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging

(b) PATH 3 — HOOKS injection (shipped): `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` on SessionStart / SubagentStart / UserPromptSubmit / UserPromptExpansion / PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop etc. SessionStart additionally supports `initialUserMessage` (non-interactive `-p` only; becomes the first user turn) and `sessionTitle`. Plain stdout on UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart/PostModelSwitch is also added as context. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks

(b) PATH 4 — AGENT SDK (Python/TypeScript, shipped): `query(prompt)` or `ClaudeSDKClient.query()` accept a string or an async iterable of `SDKUserMessage` dicts (streaming input mode); sessions support `resume`, `fork_session`, `resume_session_at`, `session_store` mirroring. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/python ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/streaming-vs-single-mode

(b) PATH 5 — HEADLESS/PRINT MODE (shipped): `claude -p "<prompt>"`, stdin piping (10MB cap), `--output-format text|json|stream-json`, `--json-schema`, `--bare`, `--continue` / `--resume <session-id>`. Notably `--cloud <session-id> -p` 'queues a message into that cloud session and exits' — an external write into a cloud session. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless

(b) PATH 6 — IDE INTEGRATION (shipped, but no message-injection API): the VS Code extension runs a local MCP server named `ide` over unencrypted `ws://` on 127.0.0.1, random port 10000-65535, authenticated by a token in `~/.claude/ide/.lock` sent as `X-Claude-Code-Ide-Authorization`. Only two tools are model-visible (`mcp__ide__getDiagnostics`, `mcp__ide__executeCode`); the rest is internal RPC for the CLI's own UI. The CLI attaches the editor selection and active-file path as context to each prompt the user sends and the transcript shows a `⧉ Selected N lines from <file>` line. There is no documented way for an external process to submit a message. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ide-integrations

(b) PATH 7 — REMOTE CONTROL (shipped): drive a local session from claude.ai or the Claude mobile app; listed as the feature for 'steering an in-progress session while away from your desk', contrasted with channels. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels

(b) NO first-class 'inject a prompt into a running session' API exists. Anthropic feature requests covering exactly this were all CLOSED: `claude inject` #24947, inter-agent message injection #27441 (closed duplicate), deterministic external inbox injection semantics #27545 (closed stale), `claude-vscode.sendMessage` #27873 (closed duplicate). The issue bodies themselves state 'there is no API, socket, or pipe to inject a prompt into an active session' and list tmux `send-keys` / one-shot `-p` subprocesses as the workarounds. https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27441 ; https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27545 ; https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27873

(c) THE CENTRAL ANSWER: Claude Code has NO assistant-authored or system-authored injection path into the conversation. Every injected item is a USER-ROLE message, but it carries a first-class provenance tag. The TS SDK reference states it explicitly: `SDKMessageOrigin` = 'Provenance of a user-role message. This appears as `origin` on `SDKUserMessage` and is forwarded onto the corresponding `SDKResultMessage` so you can tell what triggered a given turn.' https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript

(c) The full origin taxonomy (TS SDK reference): `{kind:"human"}`, `{kind:"channel", server}`, `{kind:"peer", from, fromMode?, name?, fromSession?, senderTaskId?, body?, verifiedPeerPid?}`, `{kind:"task-notification", subkind?, fireReason?, runId?}` (subkinds `scheduled-trigger`, `peer-send-message`), `{kind:"coordinator"}`, `{kind:"auto-continuation"}`, `{kind:"unclassified"}`. Human-only checks (the `ultracode` workflow keyword) REJECT a user message with no `origin`: 'Claude Code treats a user message with no `origin` as unattributed'. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript

(c) DIRECT MAPPING TO THE TWO VERBS. 'Silent note' ≈ `shouldQuery: false` on an SDKUserMessage: 'set it to `false` to append the message to the transcript without triggering an assistant turn. The message is held and merged into the next user message that does trigger a turn. Use this to inject context, such as the output of a command you ran out of band, without spending a model call on it.' Also matches hook `additionalContext`. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript

(c) 'Visible say' ≈ a normal SDKUserMessage (a user turn that starts/continues a turn), a channel event, or a peer `SendMessage` — all user-role, all attributed via `origin`. Mid-turn timing is controlled by `priority: 'now'|'next'|'later'`; `'now'` with `origin {kind:"human"}` moves backgroundable work aside (v2.1.286+), `'now'` without that origin interrupts the turn. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript

(c) Other provenance flags on SDKUserMessage: `client_composed: true` = deliver text verbatim (no `@path`/`@server:resource` expansion, no `/command` dispatch; set on every message by the `verbatimPrompts` option, 'use this option when your prompt text includes content the end user didn't type'); `isSynthetic: true` = 'marks a message as not typed by the user'; `pasted_content` / `inline_pastes` = content pasted rather than typed, possibly wrapped in `<pasted_content>` tags. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/python

(c) Injected turns are surfaced to SDK clients as replays: `SDKUserMessageReplay` — 'A user turn injected from outside the session, one whose `origin` kind is `peer` or `channel`, reaches the stream as a replay whether it was delivered during an active turn or started a new turn while the session was idle.' https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript

(c) TRANSCRIPT RENDERING — hooks = invisible system reminder. 'Claude Code wraps the string in a system reminder and inserts it into the conversation at the point where the hook fired. Claude reads the reminder on the next model request, but it doesn't appear as a chat message in the interface.' At UserPromptSubmit: 'Neither channel produces a visible transcript entry... each injected as a system reminder that starts with the hook's name.' The injected text IS written to the session transcript and replayed on resume rather than re-running the hook. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks

(c) TRANSCRIPT RENDERING — channels = an attributed inbound line, not a user bubble. 'The terminal shows it as an inbound channel line like `← fakechat · web: what's in my working directory?`, while the model receives it as a `<channel source="...">` event, using the plugin's scoped server name.' Tag attributes come from the notification's `meta` map. Channel events carry `origin.kind = "channel"` with the source MCP server name. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference

(c) TRANSCRIPT RENDERING — peer messages = a dim attributed preview. 'Claude Code shows it in the conversation as a dim one-line preview, and the preview line stays in the conversation afterward... such as `› Message from @api-worker: Schema migration finished (ctrl+o to expand)`.' Ctrl+O opens the transcript viewer; `--verbose` shows full text. The receiving Claude is told the message came from another session, NOT from the user, and it 'limits what the message can do' (cannot approve permissions, cannot change config, `/compact`-style commands arrive as plain text and never execute). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging

(c) Channels do not appear as ordinary user messages in the CLI either: `getSessionMessages()` had to be fixed to stop omitting 'messages from other agents, sessions and channels that the CLI transcript shows' — i.e. peer/channel turns ARE persisted in the CLI transcript but are a distinct class from typed prompts. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/main/CHANGELOG.md

(c) SDK changelog wording confirms the provenance model as a deliberate feature: 'Message origin on `UserMessage` and `ResultMessage`: New `origin: MessageOrigin | None` field ... surfaces why a turn was initiated — distinguishing application-submitted prompts ("human") from background-task notifications, scheduled triggers, peer messages, and other session-injected turns'. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/CHANGELOG.md

(d) ACP IS THIRD-PARTY (Zed Industries), NOT an Anthropic protocol. ACP is published at agentclientprotocol.com and owned by the `agentclientprotocol` GitHub org (created 2025-09-30). Zed's launch post says 'our new Agent Client Protocol (ACP)... ACP is our new open standard that lets any agent connect to Zed (and other editors, too).' https://github.com/agentclientprotocol ; https://zed.dev/blog/claude-code-via-acp

(d) Claude Code's ACP support is an adapter AROUND the Anthropic SDK, not native. The ACP Agents page lists 'Claude Agent (via Zed's SDK adapter)'; the adapter repo is `agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` ('Use Claude Agent SDK from any ACP client', formerly `zed-industries/claude-code-acp`, Apache-2.0). Anthropic's own feature request for native ACP (anthropics/claude-code#6686) was CLOSED on 2026-02-19 with no native implementation; a Zed team member commented 'Let the Anthropic team know if you'd like native support with no adapters!', and an in-thread analysis notes native support 'would place the maintenance burden directly on the Anthropic team to track and implement a third-party protocol.' https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/agents.md ; https://github.com/agentclientprotocol ; https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/6686

(d) ACP's write verb is user-only and has no provenance concept. A turn begins when the Client sends `session/prompt` carrying a User Message (text / resource / image content); the Agent reports output back via `session/update` notifications (plan, agent_message_chunk, tool_call, usage_update). There is no ACP method for injecting assistant- or system-authored content into a session, and no `origin`-style attribution field. ACP v2 is in Draft (v2 Prompt Lifecycle, v2 overview), with RFDs for session-fork, subagent sessions, MCP-over-ACP, etc. https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/prompt-turn.md ; https://agentclientprotocol.com/llms.txt

(d) ACP is nowhere in Anthropic's own docs: no Claude Code or Agent SDK documentation page references the Agent Client Protocol or ships native ACP support; the ecosystem page is third-party. ACP also lists many non-Anthropic agents (Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, OpenHands, JetBrains Junie, and 'Hermes Agent'). https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/agents.md
shipped_status: SHIPPED (Anthropic, first-party): voice DICTATION only (/voice in the CLI and VS Code extension; input-only, no spoken replies; requires a claude.ai sign-in and a local mic; audio streamed to Anthropic servers) — docs.claude.com/voice-dictation; full-duplex voice mode exists only in the Claude chatbot apps, explicitly NOT in Claude Code ('In Claude Cowork and Claude Code, dictation is available but voice mode isn't', support.claude.com/en/articles/11101966). SHIPPED injection ingress: (1) MCP channels — push events into a running session, research preview, `--channels`, Anthropic-auth and org-gated; (2) cross-session messaging — `ListAgents`/`SendMessage` plus a per-session inbox Unix socket exported as CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET/CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN, documented for scripts/hooks to post into a session; (3) hooks `additionalContext`; (4) the Agent SDK's SDKUserMessage with `shouldQuery`, `origin`, `priority`, `client_composed`, `isSynthetic`; (5) headless `claude -p` and `--cloud <session-id> -p`; (6) the VS Code extension's local `ide` MCP server (internal RPC, no message-submit API); (7) Remote Control from claude.ai/mobile. NOT SHIPPED: a first-class external 'inject a prompt into a running session' API (requests #24947, #27441, #27545, #27873 all closed duplicate/stale) and native ACP support in Claude Code (#6686 closed). THIRD-PARTY ONLY: ACP (Zed Industries) and the claude-agent-acp adapter wrapping the Anthropic SDK; all TTS/read-aloud for Claude Code (Stop-hook projects; read-aloud feature request #79542 open).
ui_surface: Claude Code surface, three distinct renderings for three producers. (1) Typed/dictated user input renders as a normal user turn in the prompt/transcript — voice dictation is indistinguishable from typing because it writes into the same prompt buffer; the IDE adds a `⧉ Selected N lines from <file>` context line to that same user prompt. (2) Hook-injected context renders NOWHERE as a chat message: it is a system reminder inserted at the hook's firing point, visible to the model on the next request but absent from the interface; the injected text is still persisted in the session transcript. (3) Channel and peer turns render as their OWN attributed, distinct one-line entries and are never shown as user bubbles: channels as an inbound line `← fakechat · web: <first line of message>` (model sees a `<channel source="...">` tag with meta attributes), peers as a dim preview `› Message from @api-worker: <text> (ctrl+o to expand)` expandable via Ctrl+O / click / `--verbose`. Assistant output returns as normal assistant turns; channels reply outbound through an MCP reply tool; peer replies via SendMessage. Distinguishability therefore comes from a dedicated attributed line plus transcript provenance metadata (`origin` kind), NOT from a distinct message role. In the DSH plugin's terms: Claude Code's 'silent note' is a hook system-reminder-style injection with no visible entry; its 'visible say' is a user-role turn carrying an `origin` tag and rendered as an attributed system/bridge line, not as the human speaking.
unverified: Claude Code desktop app voice dictation details: a user-report issue (#90576, open, filed 2026-08-29) states the macOS desktop app (v2.1.247) has a click-only mic button and that `/voice` returns "isn't available in this environment". This is a user claim, not Anthropic documentation — the /voice-dictation doc names only the CLI and the VS Code extension as dictation surfaces. Treat the desktop app's dictation surface as UNVERIFIED.

Whether a CHANNEL event can be injected without starting a turn (a true silent note). Channels are documented as events Claude reacts to (and queue into the next turn when busy), but the channels/channels-reference pages do not document a `shouldQuery:false`-style non-turn mode. The channel event appears in SDK streams with `origin.kind = "channel"` (inferred from `SDKUserMessageReplay` covering kinds `peer` and `channel`), but the exact transcript record for a channel event is not shown in the primary docs — UNVERIFIED.

The exact wrapper tag for cross-session peer messages delivered over the socket: Anthropic's released SendMessage tool prompt text (seen only in third-party mirrors of the CLI source) says 'Your message arrives wrapped as `<...>`', with the tag name truncated in the retrieved copy. The primary docs describe the message as arriving 'as plain text' with a sender name and reply address. Exact tag name UNVERIFIED.

Whether the Claude Code CHANGELOG (raw anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md) documents the voice dictation launch or the channels launch: the retrieved 541-line CHANGELOG covers 2.1.292 downward and contained no visible 'voice'/'channel'/'inject'/'ACP' entries in the text returned, so release-note-level attribution for those features is UNVERIFIED (the feature docs themselves are primary and dated by content).

ACP technical implementation risk claimed by a commenter (not Anthropic or Zed): 'Native ACP support in Claude Code would still be a good thing, since it would eliminate the lost in translation errors' and separate claims that the SDKs lack feature parity with the interactive CLI. Community opinion, UNVERIFIED.

The claim that claude.ai/Cowork voice mode is 'full two-way' is documented for the Claude apps; whether any of that is reusable from a Claude Code session is not documented — no Claude Code API exposes TTS or a spoken-reply channel. UNVERIFIED as non-existent vs merely undocumented: there is no primary source asserting a Claude Code TTS surface.

Nothing in Anthropic's docs states that MCP channels, cross-session messaging, or the SDK are intended as a supported ingress for third-party voice clients; the mapping of those mechanisms to a voice producer identity is this report's analysis, not an Anthropic-documented design.
